catalog_quote: Pamela Munro (MUNRO, 1977) ha restituido para el protoyutonahua un acento rítmico que caía sobre las moras de orden par. En nuestro campo, la evolución subsecuente dió origen a tres sistemas acentuales distintos. a. En tubar, el acento tónico cae siempre en la última sílaba de la palabra. En los demás grupos el acento tiene, en los morfemas raíces que son generalmente disílabos, una posición básica: de ésta se desplaza solamente en ciertos compuestos, siempre de una sílaba a la que sigue. ... b. En tarahumar-varojío, la posición básica del acento coincide por lo regular con la segunda sílaba de la raíz. c. En los demás grupos, parece que la posición básica del acento coincide con la primera sílaba de la raíz. new_statements.translation: Pamela Munro (1977) has reconstructed for Proto-Uto-Aztecan a rhythmic accent that fell on even-numbered moras. In our area, the subsequent evolution gave rise to three distinct accent systems. a. In Tubar, the tonic accent always falls on the last syllable of the word. In the other groups the accent has, in root morphemes (which are generally disyllabic), a basic position, from which it shifts only in certain compounds, always by one syllable to the following one.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of the word (Lionnet's summary table: 'Sílaba tónica' = last, contrasting with first-syllable stress in Tepiman, Opata-Eudeve and Cahita and second-syllable stress in Tarahumara-Guarijío).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Tubar: 'siempre' (always). The remark about stress shifting in certain compounds applies to the other Sonoran groups, not Tubar.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('última sílaba de la palabra'). The language is extinct; Lionnet's generalization rests on his 1978 analysis of Carl Lumholtz's 1890s field notes (and Hartman's), i.e. transcribed wordlist/citation forms, not on modern instrumental or fieldwork data. Statement is made in a comparative article by the author of the only grammatical description (Lionnet 1978), which was not opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Tubar proper (tuba1279, ISO tbu), an extinct Sonoran Uto-Aztecan language of the Río Fuerte area (San Miguel / San Andrés near Morelos, Chihuahua). No dialects distinguished; all linguistic data go back to Carl Lumholtz's 1890s notes (plus C.V. Hartman's), edited by Lionnet 1978. Lionnet 1985 abbreviates it TR.

sources.note: Section 1 'Desplazamiento del acento tónico' (PDF p. 5): 'En tubar, el acento tónico cae siempre en la última sílaba de la palabra'; summary table (PDF p. 4) row 'Sílaba tónica' gives TR (Tubar) = Última, vs. Primera for Tepiman/Opata-Eudeve/Cahita and Segunda for Tarahumara-Guarijío. Author is the same Lionnet who wrote the 1978 Tubar description (his ref. LIONNET 1978a).

Glottolog lists only overview/ethnographic refs (Lumholtz 1902; Adelung & Vater 1816; Marietti 1870; Hervás 1787; Lionnet 1978 tagged ethnographic) and no descriptive-status source. WALS cites only Lionnet 1978 and codes no stress features.
